title: Negation
rule: In standard written French, put ne before the conjugated verb and pas after it. Ne becomes n’ before a vowel sound, including a silent h. Keep the rest of the sentence in place.
example: Je ne parle pas français. · Elle n’habite pas ici.
aside: You will often hear ne dropped in conversation. Here, practise the standard written form. These examples keep definite articles such as le and la unchanged.

exercises.instruction: Make this negative in standard written French.

alternatives.message: That is common in casual speech. This written-form exercise asks for ne before parle as well as pas after it.

exercises.hint: The verb is parle. Put ne before it and pas after it.
exercises.feedback: Check that both parts of the written negation surround the conjugated verb.
exercises.explanation: Ne and pas surround the conjugated verb parle. Français keeps its cedilla.

exercises.instruction: Build the negative version in standard written French.
answers: Vous ne regardez pas la télé.
exercises.hint: Begin with Vous ne regardez. Pas follows the verb.
exercises.feedback: Keep the subject first and the object together. The verb belongs between the two parts of the negation.
exercises.explanation: Ne comes before regardez and pas comes after it. The definite article la does not change.

exercises.instruction: Fill the blank to make the sentence negative in standard written French. Write only the missing word.
exercises.hint: Ne is already before travailles. What belongs after the verb?
exercises.feedback: The first part of the negation is already present. Supply its partner after the verb.
exercises.explanation: The two parts of the negation surround travailles: ne travailles pas.

exercises.instruction: Fix the word order without changing the meaning.
exercises.hint: Travaillons is the verb. Put it between ne and pas.
exercises.feedback: The two parts of the negation should not sit together before the verb.
exercises.explanation: The order is subject, ne, conjugated verb, pas: Nous ne travaillons pas.

exercises.instruction: Make this negative in standard written French.

alternatives.message: That is common in casual speech. In the requested written form, add n’ before écoute.

exercises.hint: Écoute starts with a vowel sound. Use n’ before it and pas after it.
exercises.feedback: Check both the placement of the negation and the elision before the vowel sound.
exercises.explanation: The vowel sound at the start of écoute requires n’ rather than ne. La radio stays unchanged.

exercises.instruction: Build the negative version in standard written French.
exercises.hint: Aimes begins with a vowel sound, so n’ joins directly to it.
exercises.feedback: The apostrophe tile must join directly to the verb. Keep the object after the negation.
exercises.explanation: Ne shortens to n’ before aimes. Pas follows the verb, and the definite article le stays unchanged.

exercises.instruction: Fill the blank with the missing part of the written negation. Include the apostrophe.
exercises.hint: The next word, aimons, starts with a vowel sound.
exercises.feedback: The next word begins with a vowel sound. The missing part needs an apostrophe.
exercises.explanation: Ne becomes n’ before aimons. The apostrophe joins n’ directly to the verb.

exercises.instruction: Fix the written negation. Keep the other words unchanged.
exercises.source: Je ne aime pas le froid.
exercises.hint: Aime begins with a vowel sound. Shorten ne.
exercises.feedback: The negation is in the right position, but its first part must elide before a vowel sound.
exercises.explanation: The e of ne disappears before aime and is replaced by an apostrophe. Pas is already in the right place.

exercises.instruction: Make this negative in standard written French. Habiter has a silent h.

alternatives.message: That is common in casual speech. For this written-form exercise, include n’ before habite.

exercises.hint: A silent h allows the same elision as a vowel: n’habite.
exercises.feedback: Remember both parts of the written negation. The silent h affects the form of the first part.
exercises.explanation: The h in habiter is silent, so ne becomes n’. Not every French word beginning with h allows this elision.

exercises.instruction: Build the negative version in standard written French. Hésiter has a silent h.
exercises.hint: Begin with Il n’hésite. Put pas after the verb.
exercises.feedback: Keep the subject first. The silent h allows the apostrophe tile to join directly to the verb.
exercises.explanation: Hésiter means to hesitate. Its silent h allows n’hésite, just as a vowel allows n’aime.

exercises.instruction: Fill the blank with the missing part of the written negation. Habiter has a silent h; include the apostrophe.
exercises.hint: Use the shortened form of ne before habites.
exercises.feedback: Treat the silent h like a vowel sound when choosing the missing form.
exercises.explanation: The silent h in habites allows elision. N’ goes immediately before the verb and pas immediately after it.

exercises.instruction: Fix the written negation. Hésiter has a silent h; keep the other words unchanged.
exercises.hint: A silent h lets ne shorten to n’.
exercises.feedback: The silent h requires elision. Change the first part of the negation, not the verb.
exercises.explanation: The h in hésitons is silent, so ne must elide. Pas already follows the conjugated verb.

title: Questions
description: Ask a question while keeping familiar word order.
rule: Put est-ce que before a statement to make a yes-or-no question. Keep the normal subject–verb order. Que becomes qu’ before a vowel sound, as in est-ce qu’elle.
example: Tu parles français. → Est-ce que tu parles français ?
aside: Inversion and rising intonation are also valid ways to ask questions. These exercises specifically practise est-ce que, or est-ce qu’ before a vowel sound.

exercises.instruction: Turn this statement into a question using est-ce que.

alternatives.message: That is valid French using inversion. This exercise asks for est-ce que with tu before parles.
That is a valid question with rising intonation in speech. This exercise asks you to add est-ce que.

exercises.hint: Add Est-ce que at the beginning. Keep tu before parles.
exercises.feedback: Use the requested question opening, then keep the statement’s subject before its verb.
exercises.explanation: Est-ce que introduces the question without changing the order of tu parles.

exercises.instruction: Build the question using est-ce que.
exercises.hint: Start with Est-ce que, then vous venez.
exercises.feedback: The question opening comes first. After it, keep the same subject–verb order as the statement.
exercises.explanation: After est-ce que, the statement’s normal subject–verb order stays unchanged.

exercises.instruction: Complete the question with the missing word from est-ce que. Write only that word.
exercises.hint: Nous begins with a consonant sound, so use the full form que.
exercises.feedback: Complete the fixed question opening. The following consonant sound does not require elision.
exercises.explanation: Que stays complete before nous. The subject nous remains before the verb partons.

exercises.instruction: Fix the word order after est-ce que. Keep all the words.
exercises.hint: After est-ce que, put the subject tu before the verb parles.
exercises.feedback: The question opening is already present. Check whether the subject comes before the verb.
exercises.explanation: Est-ce que uses normal subject–verb order. Inversion is a separate question form, not an extra step after est-ce que.

exercises.instruction: Turn this statement into a question using est-ce que, shortened where needed.

alternatives.message: That is valid French using inversion. This exercise asks for est-ce qu’elle followed by aime.
That is a valid question with rising intonation in speech. Here, use the requested est-ce qu’ form.

exercises.hint: Elle begins with a vowel sound, so que becomes qu’.
exercises.feedback: Use the requested question opening and check its elision before the subject’s vowel sound.
exercises.explanation: Que elides before elle. The subject elle still comes before the verb aime.

exercises.instruction: Build the question using the shortened form of est-ce que.
exercises.hint: Join Est-ce qu’ to ils, then keep habitent ici in order.
exercises.feedback: Join the apostrophe-ending opening to the subject, then keep the verb after the subject.
exercises.explanation: Que becomes qu’ because the next word is ils, which begins with a vowel sound.

exercises.instruction: Fill the blank with que or its shortened form. Write only the missing part, including any apostrophe.
exercises.hint: Il starts with a vowel sound, so drop the e of que.
exercises.feedback: The following pronoun starts with a vowel sound. Include the apostrophe in the shortened form.
exercises.explanation: Que becomes qu’ immediately before il. The apostrophe joins the two without a space.

exercises.instruction: Fix the elision in this question. Keep the other words unchanged.
exercises.hint: Elles starts with a vowel sound. Shorten que before it.
exercises.feedback: The subject–verb order is correct. Check the elision immediately before the subject.
exercises.explanation: Que must elide before elles. The order elles arrivent is already correct.

exercises.instruction: Turn this statement into a question using est-ce que. Keep the noun subject.
answers: Est-ce que le train arrive demain ?

alternatives.message: That is valid French using inversion. This exercise asks you to put est-ce que before le train arrive demain.
That is a valid question with rising intonation in speech. This exercise specifically asks for est-ce que.

exercises.hint: Put Est-ce que before the whole statement. Le train remains before arrive.
exercises.feedback: Keep the complete noun subject before its verb and add the requested opening before both.
exercises.explanation: The same pattern works with a noun subject: est-ce que, then le train, then arrive.

exercises.instruction: Build the question using est-ce que. Keep the noun subject.
answers: Est-ce que la porte est ouverte ?
exercises.hint: After Est-ce que, put the subject la porte before the verb est.
exercises.feedback: The two-word noun subject belongs between the question opening and the verb.
exercises.explanation: Est-ce que adds a question opening; it does not reverse the statement’s subject and verb.

exercises.instruction: Write the missing question opening: est-ce que or its shortened form.
exercises.hint: The next word is le, so que keeps its e.
exercises.feedback: Supply the complete question opening. Its final word is followed by a consonant sound.
exercises.explanation: Que is followed by le, not by café. There is no elision, and le café stays before est.

exercises.instruction: Fix the word order after est-ce que. Keep l’enfant as the subject and keep all the words.
exercises.hint: Put the complete subject l’enfant before joue.
exercises.feedback: Keep the noun subject together and place it before the verb, just as in a statement.
exercises.explanation: L’enfant stays together as the subject. Que does not elide here because the next sound is the l in l’enfant.

title: Adjective agreement
description: Make the describing word match the noun.
rule: Adjectives agree with the noun’s gender and number. A feminine form often adds e; a plural often adds s. For the regular adjectives here, feminine plural adds both: petit, petite, petits, petites. These spelling patterns are not universal.
example: un petit sac · une petite maison · des petits sacs · des petites maisons
aside: Un marks masculine singular; une marks feminine singular. Des marks plural but does not tell you the gender, so these exercises name it when needed. Keep the adjective in the position shown.

exercises.instruction: Replace un sac with une chaussure and make noir agree. Write the whole phrase.
exercises.hint: Une tells you chaussure is feminine singular. Add e to noir.
exercises.feedback: The new noun is feminine singular. Check the adjective’s ending as well as the noun replacement.
exercises.explanation: Changing the noun to the feminine chaussure requires noire. The adjective keeps its place after the noun.

exercises.instruction: Build the phrase with the correct form of rond. Table is feminine singular. Leave the other adjective tiles unused.
exercises.hint: Use the feminine form ronde after table.
exercises.feedback: Choose just one adjective tile. It must match a feminine noun with only one item.
exercises.explanation: Rond gains e for the feminine singular noun table. Une also shows that the noun is feminine singular.

exercises.instruction: Fill the blank with the correct form of petit. Write only the adjective.
exercises.hint: Une tells you maison is feminine singular.
exercises.feedback: Check the adjective’s feminine ending. The noun is singular, so no plural ending is needed.
exercises.explanation: Petit gains e to agree with the feminine singular noun maison. It stays before the noun in this phrase.

exercises.instruction: Fix the adjective so it agrees with voiture. Keep the other words unchanged.
exercises.hint: Une shows feminine singular. What is the feminine form of vert?
exercises.feedback: The article shows feminine singular. Make the adjective match those two features.
exercises.explanation: Verte is the feminine singular form of vert. There is one car, so do not add a plural s.

exercises.instruction: Make the whole phrase plural, replacing un with des. Sac is masculine.
exercises.hint: Both petit and sac gain s in the plural.
exercises.feedback: Make both the noun and adjective plural, and replace the singular article as requested.
exercises.explanation: Petits agrees with the masculine plural noun sacs. No feminine e is needed.

exercises.instruction: Build the phrase with the correct form of vert. Livres is masculine plural. Leave the other adjective tiles unused.
exercises.hint: The adjective needs a plural s but no feminine e.
exercises.feedback: Choose just one adjective tile. It must be plural without a feminine ending.
exercises.explanation: Vert becomes verts to describe more than one masculine livre.

exercises.instruction: Fill the blank with the correct form of noir. Sacs is masculine plural. Write only the adjective.
exercises.hint: Start with noir and add the regular plural ending.
exercises.feedback: The noun is masculine and names more than one item. Check both features of your adjective.
exercises.explanation: The adjective agrees with masculine plural sacs, so noir gains s but not e.

exercises.instruction: Fix only the adjective. Chats is masculine plural.
exercises.hint: Chats already has its plural s. Give noir one too.
exercises.feedback: The noun is already plural. Check whether the adjective also marks the plural.
exercises.explanation: Noirs agrees with masculine plural chats. Des alone does not show gender; the prompt supplies it.

exercises.instruction: Make the whole phrase plural, replacing une with des. Maison is feminine.
exercises.hint: Petite already has the feminine e. Add s to both petite and maison.
exercises.feedback: Keep the adjective feminine while making both it and the noun plural. Remember to change the article.
exercises.explanation: Petites agrees with feminine plural maisons. Its ending has both e for feminine and s for plural.

exercises.instruction: Build the phrase with the correct form of rond. Tables is feminine plural. Leave the other adjective tiles unused.
exercises.hint: The adjective needs both the feminine e and the plural s.
exercises.feedback: Choose just one adjective tile. Its ending must show both feminine and plural.
exercises.explanation: Rond becomes rondes for feminine plural tables: add e, then s.

exercises.instruction: Fill the blank with the correct form of vert. Voitures is feminine plural. Write only the adjective.
exercises.hint: Use the feminine form verte, then make it plural.
exercises.feedback: Check both gender and number: the noun is feminine and refers to more than one item.
exercises.explanation: Vertes matches both the feminine gender and the plural number of voitures.

exercises.instruction: Fix only the adjective. Chaussures is feminine plural.
exercises.hint: Noir must match both feminine and plural.
exercises.feedback: The adjective must reflect two features of the noun: feminine gender and plural number.
exercises.explanation: Noires has the feminine e and the plural s required by chaussures.
